items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: And the drummer was Little Mac... I think his last name was Robinson... Yes, yes. And the drummer was Little Mac, Mud Carey on the trumpet.

ctx.x: Robinson. There was once a Mac Murray there. Yeah. And then I've heard of a Mac Hill that Lee Collins has told me about. It wouldn't be Mac Hill. Oh, no, no, no, no. I didn't know any of those fellas myself, personally. Well, they all were kids. But Roberts. You think it was Mac Robertson? I think
it was Mac Robertson because- Or Robinson or Robertson? Robinson. Robinson.

Yeah, if I'm not sure. Because we'd call him Little Mac. Little Mac, yes. I've heard him call. Yeah. And then we had Steve Lewis. On piano. Yes. Steve Lewis was on piano. Johnny Dodds on clarinet, and Mud Carey on the cornet. Well, who was a trombone player? Well, at that time, he only brought four. That's what Mud told me. Only four pieces that you came up. And we were the first company that had the jazz band on the stage, isn't it? That's right, yes. On the stage. Not down in the pit, we put them on the stage.…
